'''Host Europe Group''' (formerly '''Pipex Communications plc''' and '''GX Networks''') was an American-owned, European-located [[Web hosting service|website hosting]], [[email hosting service|email]] and [[domain name registrar]] company headquartered [[Hayes, Hillingdon|Hayes]], [[West London]]. Founded as GX Networks in 1997, the company was renamed Pipex Communications plc following its takeover of [[Pipex]] in 2003.<ref name=":1" /> It reverted to the GX Networks name following its sale of Pipex in 2008<ref>{{cite news|last1=Turner|first1=Brian|url=http://www.techwatch.co.uk/2008/03/05/pipex-renamed-gx-networks/|title=Pipex renamed GX Networks|date=5 March 2008|work=Techwatch|accessdate=13 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Nixon|first1=Dave|url=http://www.techwatch.co.uk/2008/03/09/previous-divisions-of-pipex-group-become-gx-networks/|title=Previous divisions of Pipex group become GX Networks|date=9 March 2008|work=Techwatch|accessdate=13 January 2015}}</ref> before being renamed Host Europe Group in 2009.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Judge |first=Peter |title=Host Europe buys Germany's Intergenia |url=https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/host-europe-buys-germanys-intergenia/ |access-date=2020-02-11 |website=www.datacenterdynamics.com |date=19 December 2014 |language=en}}</ref> It was acquired by American hosting company [[GoDaddy]] in 2017, and {{As of|2019||df=|lc=y}} its name was in the process of being phased out.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heg.com/|title=Welcome to HEG - Inspiring Next Generation Businesses|last=|first=|date=|website=HEG|language=en-GB|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190928214745/https://www.heg.com/|archive-date=2019-09-28|access-date=2016-03-22}}</ref>

==Brands==
Through a series of acquisitions and (de)mergers ''GX Networks'' (and subsequently Webfusion) is known through various brands. Since 2009, the company has consolidated its trading under the brand names: [[123-reg]] (The UK's largest domain name registrar, with more than 3 million names registered and 1.3 million websites hosted),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rego |first=Sara |title=About 123 Reg {{!}} Unlock the full power of the web |url=https://www.123-reg.co.uk/about-us/ |access-date=2024-03-10 |website=123 Reg |language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Heart Internet]] (UK hosting), Tsohost (UK hosting), Host Europe (German hosting), Webfusion (Spanish hosting), RedCoruna (Spanish hosting), Mesh Digital and Domainbox (international domain names).<ref>{{cite web|title=Our Brands|url=http://www.hosteuropegroup.com/webfusion/|work=Host Europe Group|accessdate=24 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120809024746/http://www.hosteuropegroup.com/webfusion/|archive-date=2012-08-09|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==History==
Host Europe was founded by [[Cologne]]-based entrepreneur Uwe Braun.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=W. F. |date=12 January 2022 |title=Disclose.tv: Conspiracy Forum Turned Disinformation Factory |url=https://www.logically.ai/articles/disclose.tv-conspiracy-forum-turned-disinformation-factory |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220112153617/https://www.logically.ai/articles/disclose.tv-conspiracy-forum-turned-disinformation-factory |archive-date=12 January 2022 |access-date=9 July 2023 |website=[[Logically (company)|Logically]] |language=en |quote=Uwe Braun is an entrepreneur based in Cologne, Germany who has made millions in internet hosting businesses. His company Host Europe was sold for 1.68 billion euros in late 2016.}}</ref> It began by offering internet services to corporations and began trading under the GX name in 1997. It believed that it had developed the first transatlantic IP backbone running native [[Asynchronous Transfer Mode|ATM]].{{citation needed|date=July 2012}}<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/tr/pdf/ADA330111.pdf|title=TRANSPORT FLOW CONTROL AND CONNECTION ADMISSION POLICIES FOR RELIABLE APPLICATIONS}}</ref> Webfusion originally started out with major Network Access Points in [[Washington (U.S. state)|Washington]] and [[San Jose, California|San Jose]] in the US, [[London]]'s [[LINX]] and [[Stockholm]] in Europe.

With various changes of ownership, the company's name has changed several times, taking on the [[Pipex]] name following its takeover in 2003. Following restructuring in 2009, the company trades under the Webfusion name in the UK, as part of HEG (formerly Host Europe Group), and is based in [[Hayes, Hillingdon|Hayes]] in [[West London]]. As of 2015, HEG claimed to be Europe's largest privately owned hosting company.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.megabuyte.com/reports/56e28e51e4b0e8ab5ccf1f2f/heg-hosting-europes-smes|title=HEG: Hosting Europe's SMEs {{!}} Megabuyte|last=|first=|date=2015-11-17|website=www.megabuyte.com|access-date=2016-09-08}}</ref>

* April 1997 – Internet Technology Group (ITG) announces the acquisition of [[Xara Networks]] Limited in a deal worth £2.65 million.<ref name="autogenerated2">{{Cite web |title=Best WordPress Hosting of 2024 |url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/best-wordpress-hosting-2024-rick-hemmings-hi41e |access-date=2024-03-10 |website=www.linkedin.com |language=en}}</ref>
* September 1997 – Xara Networks, a subsidiary of Internet Technology Group (ITG), relaunched as GX Networks.<ref name=autogenerated2 />
*January 2000 – GX Networks became part of [[Concentric Network]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2001-04-05 |title=GX Networks |url=http://www.gxn.net/ |access-date=2024-03-10 |archive-date=2001-04-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010405102028/http://www.gxn.net/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_pwwi/is_200001/ai_mark02001012 Concentric Network Closes Internet Technology Group PLC Acquisition]</ref>
* September 2000 – [[Concentric Network]] merged with Nextlink to form [[XO Communications]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goodbye Nextlink, Hello XO - Company Business and Marketing |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0BMD/is_185_6/ai_65508813}}</ref>
* 2001 – The UK arm of [[XO Europe]] was sold off to form Transigent Limited.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pipexgroup.com/components/download.asp?id=12|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20061031232939/http://www.pipexgroup.com/components/download.asp?id=12|archive-date = 2006-10-31|title = 日韩人妻无码精品久久_国产在线视频www色_亚洲欧美日韩精品久久_某医院女厕美女如厕vod视频}}</ref>
* September 2002 – Zipcom plc acquires Transigent Limited (formerly XO Limited), the parent company of GX Networks, in a deal worth approximately £10m.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.m2.com/m2/web/story.php/200266B93F01F5757AA280256C440035F191|title=:: M2 Release ::}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sjberwin.com/events/news/date/2002/sj_berwin_represents_peter_dubens_and_laurence_blackall_on_sale_of_transigent/2002_09_27.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061029185001/http://www.sjberwin.com/events/news/date/2002/sj_berwin_represents_peter_dubens_and_laurence_blackall_on_sale_of_transigent/2002_09_27.html| title=None|archivedate=October 29, 2006}}</ref>
* October 2002 – Zipcom plc acquired the entire share capital of Transigent Limite,d the parent company of GX Networks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pipexgroup.com/pg.asp?p=1169|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061031232939/http://www.pipexgroup.com/pg.asp?p=1169|archive-date=2006-10-31|title=日韩人妻无码精品久久_国产在线视频www色_亚洲欧美日韩精品久久_某医院女厕美女如厕vod视频}}</ref>
* March 2003 – Zipcom plc changed its name to GX Networks plc.<ref name=autogenerated1 />
* July 2003 – GX Networks acquires two more telecoms business,es XTML Limited ("XTML") and Compulink Information eXchange Limited ("CIX"), which were previously part of the Telenor Business Holdings UK Limited Group ("[[Telenor]]").<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130122021746/http://www.e-consultancy.com/news-blog/151865/gx-networks-acquires-two-more-telecoms-businesses.html|title=GX Networks acquires two more telecoms businesses {{!}} Internet Marketing News and Blog {{!}} E-consultancy.com}}</ref>
* September 2003 – GX Networks buy [https://web.archive.org/web/20050414012026/http://www.firstnet-corporate.co.uk/ Firstnet Ltd] (owners of Liberty Broadband aka [[Tele2]] UK)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2003/09/03/gx_networks_buys_firstnet/|title = GX Networks buys Firstnet|website = [[The Register]]}}</ref>
* October 2003 – GX Networks plc became Pipex Communications plc to maintain the PIPEX brand after a buyout for £55m.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Richardson |first=Tim |title=GX Networks to buy Pipex for £55m |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2003/10/03/gx_networks_to_buy_pipex/ |access-date=2020-02-11 |website=www.theregister.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>
*April 2004 – Pipex Communications Plc acquires Host Europe Plc, an AIM-listed hosting solutions provider to the UK and Germany, for £31 million<ref>{{cite web| title=Pipex offers £31m cash for Host Europe | author=StockMarketWire| publisher=StockMarketWire| url=https://www.stockmarketwire.com/article/333156/Pipex-offers-31m-cash-for-Host-Europe.html | date=2 April 2004}}</ref>
* May 2005 – Pipex Communications acquires Donhost<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ispreview.co.uk/news/EEEVEpVAFZQvLDWoli.html|title=Pipex Acquire Donhost (WWW Hosting) : ISPreview UK News|website=www.ispreview.co.uk|access-date=2019-02-27}}</ref>
*2006 – Pipex Communications acquires Supanetwork, better known as SupaNames, for £2.2 million.<ref>https://daisygroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/06/109-pipex-annual-reports-and-accounts-2006.pdf#page=15{{Dead link|date=February 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
* March 2008 – Due to Pipex Broadband being sold to Tiscali (now [[TalkTalk Group|Talk Talk]]), the company known as Pipex Communications UK Ltd reverts to GX Networks Ltd.<ref>[http://www.techwatch.co.uk/2008/03/05/pipex-renamed-gx-networks/ Pipex renamed GX Networks]</ref>
* October 2009 – Further internal re-structuring by Oakley Capital (Owner of GX Networks) after selling Vialtus Solutions and further consolidating the brands of GX Networks by renaming the company Host Europe Group,<ref name=":0" /> and the UK business after the hosting branch of the firm Webfusion Limited
* March 2010 – Host Europe Group acquires Virtualization firm Vanager
* September 2010 – Host Europe Group acquired by [[Montagu Private Equity]]
* March 2011 – Host Europe Group acquires Dynamic-net.ch AG
* August 2011 – Host Europe Group acquires [[Heart Internet]] Ltd
* January 2012 – Host Europe Group acquires Spanish web host RedCoruna
* May 2012 – Dynamic-net rebrands to Host Europe Suisse
* May 2012 – Host Europe Group acquires Mesh Digital Ltd
* July 2013 – Host Europe Group is acquired by [[Cinven]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Deals of the day -- mergers and acquisitions| work=Reuters| url=https://www.reuters.com/article/deals-day-idUSL4N0FP2EM20130719| date=19 July 2013| access-date=3 July 2017| archive-date=24 September 2015| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924183158/http://www.reuters.com/article/2013/07/19/deals-day-idUSL4N0FP2EM20130719| url-status=live}}</ref>
* Oct 2013 – Host Europe Group acquires Telefónica Online Services
* Oct 2013 – Host Europe Group acquires domainFACTORY
* Aug 2014 – Host Europe Group acquires Sign-Up.to
* Nov 2014 – Host Europe Group becomes HEG
* Dec 2014 – HEG acquires intergenia AG (with subsidiaries Plusserver, Server4you, and Serverloft)
* Oct 2015 – HEG acquires Paragon Internet Group<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archived copy, HEG : Hosting and domain services |url=https://www.cinven.com/lib/docs/155242-cinvenar2015heg.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629143554/http://www.cinven.com/lib/docs/155242-cinvenar2015heg.pdf |archive-date=2017-06-29 |access-date=2017-07-16}}</ref>
* Dec 2016 – [[GoDaddy]] acquires HEG for €1.69 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Medhora |first=Narottam |date=2016-12-06 |title=GoDaddy to buy Host Europe for US$1.82 billion |url=https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/godaddy-to-buy-host-europe-for-us-1-82-billion-1.624905 |access-date=2023-07-09 |website=[[BNN Bloomberg]] |agency=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> The full list of HEG brands in 2017 can be found here.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.whtop.com/groups#heg|title=HEG brands|access-date=2017-11-01}}</ref>
* Apr 2024 – [[GoDaddy]] Divests Heart Internet <ref>{{cite web |title=GoDaddy Divests Heart Internet |url=https://aboutus.godaddy.net/newsroom/company-news/news-details/2024/GoDaddy-Divests-Heart-Internet/default.aspx#:~:text=GoDaddy%20closed%20a%20transaction%20to,United%20Kingdom%20on%20March%2028. |publisher=GoDaddy}}</ref>

extract: Host Europe Group (formerly Pipex Communications plc and GX Networks) was an American-owned, European-located website hosting, email and domain name registrar company headquartered Hayes, West London. Founded as GX Networks in 1997, the company was renamed Pipex Communications plc following its takeover of Pipex in 2003. It reverted to the GX Networks name following its sale of Pipex in 2008 before being renamed Host Europe Group in 2009. It was acquired by American hosting company GoDaddy in 2017, and as of 2019 its name was in the process of being phased out.
